compiled_state.title: Add Execution Trace Requirement to Plan and Fidelity Reviewers
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context
The evaluation paradox (Research Gap 5: LLM-as-a-Judge) means LLM reviewers suffer from verbosity bias and misclassify broken output as correct. Plan/fidelity reviewers in the brainstorm and implementation-plan skills currently score dimensions without explicitly tracing execution logic. Research (EvalPlus benchmark) shows forcing execution traces drastically reduces misclassification. Deferred from the main blindspots initiative to limit scope.

## Success Criteria
- Plan reviewers (implementation-plan Step 4) include an execution trace requirement for at least one success criterion per review
- Fidelity reviewers (brainstorm scrutiny pipeline Step 4) include an execution trace requirement
- Completion verifier includes execution-based verification steps (run verify commands, not just static assessment)

## Dependencies
None (can be implemented independently)

## Approach
TBD. Needs /dso:brainstorm before implementation (placeholder epic — scrutiny skipped).

comments.body:
Correction: prior comment on this ticket was malformed (CLI syntax error — used --body as a flag instead of positional). Disregard it.

Proposed scope addition (2026-04-26): structural sentinel as the enforcement layer beneath the existing prose-level execution-trace SCs.

Today /dso:brainstorm phases/approval-gate.md gained a one-line SCRUTINY attestation HARD-GATE (cross_epic and pipeline sub-agent IDs, or SKIPPED with reason + user authorization). That blocks the most common rationalization path (orchestrator drafts approval prose without dispatching the scrutiny pipeline), but the attestation values are still orchestrator-authored — there is no machine check that the named sub-agent IDs correspond to real dispatches.

Suggested SC to absorb here:

> Structural sentinel for fidelity / scrutiny attestation. Brainstorm approval gate (phases/approval-gate.md) and implementation-plan plan-review gate read a sentinel file (e.g., <artifacts-dir>/scrutiny-attestation-<epic-id>.json) written only by the dispatched scrutiny / fidelity / cross-epic-interaction-classifier sub-agents themselves, containing sub-agent dispatch ID, timestamp, and reviewer dimensions covered. The SCRUTINY attestation line in approval-gate.md is verified against the sentinel by a pre-prompt-render check; orchestrator-authored attestation values without a matching sentinel are rejected. This converts the prose-level execution-trace SCs in this epic into a machine-checkable structural gate.

Why here vs. a new epic: this epic's existing SCs already target 'fidelity reviewers include an execution trace requirement' and 'completion verifier includes execution-based verification steps' — both prose-level. The sentinel is the structural enforcement underneath the same intent. Approach is TBD on this epic, so absorption is clean.

Adjacent but distinct: e884-d0ad (PostToolUse hook for sub-agent attention loss) shares hook infrastructure but targets a different failure mode (orchestrator going idle after Task returns, not gate enforcement). Worth a relates_to link if both proceed.

Context for why this surfaced now: during a /dso:brainstorm session on c183-ed2a (adversarial review of inference-sourced decisions), the orchestrator (Claude) skipped the scrutiny pipeline entirely while drafting the approval gate, surfaced the skip transparently, and almost wrote the ticket. User caught it and asked for a skill edit that would have prevented the rationalization. The one-line HARD-GATE was applied to approval-gate.md as the cheap fix. This SC is the structural complement.

comments.body:
Correction / clarification (2026-04-27): the prior structural-sentinel coordination comment from 2026-04-26 referenced c183-ed2a as a single epic. On 2026-04-27 c183-ed2a was split into two epics on scrutiny review. Coordination surface is split across both halves:

- c183-ed2a (Epic A — inference channel): brainstorm Phase 1 Gate gains a completeness attestation field (SC1) and dso:red-team-reviewer gains a typed-envelope inference-challenge mode (SC2). The structural sentinel concept proposed in this epic's earlier comment applies to Phase 1 Gate's exit attestation: a sentinel artifact that the gate reads to verify the completeness attestation was actually emitted by an authorized step (not orchestrator-self-reported).

- a154-98de (Epic B — degradation channel): SC2 modifies brainstorm/phases/approval-gate.md to insert PRECONDITIONS degradation-emission bash blocks at the existing graceful-degradation prose paths. The structural sentinel concept proposed in this epic's earlier comment applies to approval-gate.md as well: the SCRUTINY: attestation line added to approval-gate.md on 2026-04-26 by the brainstorm session that surfaced this scope is the human-readable surface; this epic's structural sentinel SC would mechanically verify the attestation values against authentic sub-agent dispatches.

Both epics are now relates_to linked to this epic. When this epic implements the structural sentinel, the design must consider both attestation surfaces (Phase 1 Gate from Epic A, approval-gate.md from Epic B) in a single coordinated mechanism. When this epic and Epic B both modify approval-gate.md, the later-landing epic rebases; the sentinel insertion (this epic) and the degradation-marker insertion (Epic B) occupy non-overlapping textual regions.
